newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up 1/2 point in muted trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up 1/2 point in muted trade.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds gained from a 1/4 to a 1/2 of a point in early afternoon trade on Monday, primarily responding to even bigger gains won by Treasuries, as markets decided any inflation was benign.

"There is no inflation, everybody is talking about possible inflation, beyond the two- to two-and-a-half percent level. So I think this is just a shift in sentiment, fueled by gold, and gold sales are helping it," a trader said.

Gold has lost about 13 percent of its value so far this year under threat of selling by central banks as they reviewed the worth of holding gold reserves. The latest drop, which briefly pushed prices in London to fresh, 12-year lows, came after the Reserve Bank of Australia said last Thursday it had sold 167 tonnes of gold from its reserves.

Municipal bond traders appeared a bit more confident that the Federal Reserve will keep monetary policy on hold--perhaps not tightening rates until as far off as November, if then--and that economic data due out shortly will provide more underpinnings for this view.

Producer Prices for June are due out on July 11, and a consensus survey of economists by Reuters showed they looked for the overall reading to be unchanged, with the ex-food, energy segment expected to show a 0.1 percent gain.
Should municipal bonds keep rising, additional sales might be set, traders said, with one player speculating rates would need to fall another 20 basis or so, to draw new issues to market.
In the secondary market, Florida Ports Financing Commission Revenues of 2027, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.58 percent, NET, down four basis points.
And Delaware River Port Authority Pennsylvania and New Jersey Revenues of 2026, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 99-7/8, up three-eighths.
September Treasury bond futures leaped 24 ticks to 113-30/32, while September municipal bond futures rose 19 ticks to 119-8/32. This left the MOB spread narrower at plus 172 ticks.
Municipal bond sales this week were expected to total $2.1 billion in 99 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings added up to $1.3 billion in 41 sales, with a $150 million Sacramento Municipal Utility District, Calif., deal through Goldman, Sachs & Co., topping the list.
On the competitive side, 58 sales totaling $793 million were scheduled. A $265 million Washington deal on Wednesday is the largest.
An additional seven sales totaling $502 million were on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they might price the issues next week depending on market conditions.
